purpose: Research-only first-corpus selection; the separate approved manifest contains only the two signed sources

rubrics.reviews: JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Systematic Reviews and Research Syntheses, 2020, 11 items; yes/no/unclear judgments, not an additive score
rubrics.cohort: JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Cohort Studies, 2017, 11 items; yes/no/unclear judgments, not an additive score

pubmed_metadata_check.provider: NCBI PubMed EFetch XML over verified HTTPS
pubmed_metadata_check.scope: PublicationType and CommentsCorrections metadata; this is not an independent external retraction-index search

proposed_manifest_score_mapping.method: Use score 1.0 only for an explicitly reviewer-approved, bounded-use source; failed or unreviewed sources never enter the manifest. This encodes a binary appraisal gate, not an additive JBI score or a comparative study-quality estimate.
proposed_manifest_score_mapping.limitation: All approved first-set sources would have equal quality contribution in reranking; revise the schema and validate a comparative score before claiming quality-based ordering.

evidence: 41 population studies required structured diagnostic interviews for children younger than 13
Two-person study selection, extraction and JBI prevalence appraisal are reported
Random-effects models, prediction intervals, leave-one-out checks and GRADE are reported
limitations: No explicit protocol registration or publication-bias assessment was verified in the main text; supplementary methods need second-reviewer confirmation
The prevalence period is 2004–2019, so it cannot establish current post-pandemic rates
DMDD subgroup is sparse and its evidence was judged low quality by the authors

evidence: PROSPERO registration and six-database search are reported
24 studies and a design-specific prevalence-bias assessment are described
The authors report I-squared of 91 percent and explore some subgroups
limitations: Only 10 percent of screening, extraction and primary-study bias assessment was independently checked
No formal publication-bias assessment was verified
Depression questionnaires and diagnostic interviews were pooled; high heterogeneity makes the single pooled rate unsuitable as a general clinical prevalence claim
appraisals.recommendation: defer_from_first_ingestion; retain as candidate for carefully qualified methods/co-occurrence questions after independent review

evidence: PROSPERO registration and blinded duplicate title/abstract screening are reported
Eligibility was limited to population-based ASD samples and specified diagnostic methods
Random-effects synthesis and selected publication-bias tests are reported
limitations: A systematic per-primary-study risk-of-bias appraisal was not verified in the full text
Pooled comorbidity analyses have very high heterogeneity, generally I-squared above 84 percent
Egger's test indicated potential bias for the ADHD comorbidity subgroup; other small subgroups could not be assessed

evidence: Prospective protocol registration, multiple databases and duplicate selection/extraction are reported
31 included studies were cross-sectional and their bias was assessed with an AHRQ checklist
Subgroups and Egger's test are reported
limitations: Most primary studies did not adequately describe confounder control or missing-data handling
Ten studies supplied crude odds ratios, and depression measurement varied
The discussion sometimes calls bullying a risk factor despite cross-sectional data that cannot establish temporal or causal direction
appraisals.recommendation: exclude_from_first_ingestion; use stronger longitudinal bullying evidence for the initial corpus

evidence: Nine annual waves of a nationally representative South Korean multicultural-family panel are analyzed
Bullying and depressive symptoms use described multi-item scales; reported internal-consistency alphas are 0.85 and 0.91
Individual fixed effects and measured time-varying covariates address some confounding
limitations: Analytic sample was 1375 of 1635 baseline children after eligibility and missingness exclusions; selective follow-up was not fully resolved
Participants were not depression-free at exposure start; this is symptom-trajectory association, not incident depression
Self-report, possible reverse direction and unmeasured time-varying confounding remain; applicability beyond this population is limited

bounded_uses.37639261: Historical 2004–2019 interview-defined depressive-disorder prevalence in children younger than 13; not current or individual risk
bounded_uses.39648410: Noncausal bullying–depressive-symptom trajectories in the studied South Korean multicultural-family panel; not incident diagnosis or general-population causal risk

signoff.approval_statement: I approve PMIDs 37639261 and 39648410 for the stated bounded uses and approve the proposed score rule

next_gate: Run fresh DOI/PMID and retraction/correction checks at ingestion (and recheck within 14 days before use)
Ingest PubMed abstracts from the signed two-source manifest into both benchmark collections
Do not broaden these source uses or treat the other three appraisals as approved
